Relics of Exploration is an interactive educational website developed to explore the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars during NASA's space exploration missions.

The website features five examples: the Apollo Lunar Module Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner, and Ingenuity Mars Helicopter. Through photographs, informative profiles, search and filtering features, and an interactive quiz, users can discover the purpose of each object, its contribution to space exploration, and why it remains on the Moon or Mars.

Our project addresses the challenge by bringing attention to the often-overlooked equipment and the stories behind it. It is important because these objects represent scientific achievements, technological progress, and milestones in human exploration. We aim to make this history accessible, engaging, and educational for students and space enthusiasts.
details:
Project Details – Relics of Exploration

Relics of Exploration is an interactive educational website designed to tell the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions.

The website allows visitors to explore five examples of equipment: the Apollo Lunar Module Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner, and Ingenuity Mars Helicopter.

How It Works

Users can browse individual equipment profiles to learn about their original purpose, the missions they were part of, their scientific contributions, and why they remain on the Moon or Mars. The website includes photographs, a search feature, Moon and Mars filters, detailed information sections, and an interactive quiz to make learning more engaging.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes information about space exploration more accessible, particularly for students and people interested in science and astronomy. It draws attention to equipment that is often overlooked when discussing space missions and demonstrates how these objects contributed to scientific discoveries and technological progress.

Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space exploration and help visitors appreciate the historical and scientific importance of objects that remain beyond Earth.

Tools and Technologies Used

The website was developed using:

  • HTML: To structure the website and its content.
  • CSS: To design the layout and visual appearance.
  • JavaScript: To create interactive features such as searching, filtering, and the quiz.
  • Netlify: To publish the website online and make it accessible through a public link.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of our project is its storytelling approach. Instead of focusing only on famous missions and their achievements, we focus on the equipment left behind after those missions. We present each object's story through photographs, accessible explanations, and interactive features, turning space exploration history into an engaging learning experience.

Factors Considered During Development

While developing the project, we considered the intended audience, ease of navigation, clarity of information, visual presentation, and educational value. We aimed to make the website simple to explore while including enough historical and scientific information to help visitors understand the importance of each object.

Overall, Relics of Exploration connects the history of space missions with the physical objects that remain on the Moon and Mars, showing that the story of exploration continues even after a mission ends.
